svg.title: Direct Lake Query Path vs DirectQuery Fallback
svg.desc: A flow diagram starting from a report visual issuing a query. The query reaches the semantic model, which checks whether any requested column is already resident in memory from a prior query; if not, it loads that column lazily and directly from the OneLake Delta table, anchored to the most recent framing operation. For Direct Lake on SQL models specifically, three documented conditions — querying a SQL-endpoint view, row-level security on the SQL endpoint, or exceeding capacity guardrails — branch the query into DirectQuery fallback against the SQL analytics endpoint instead, trading the framing snapshot for live data at typically slower performance. Direct Lake on OneLake never takes this fallback branch at all. A warning node flags the specific, sourced trap of basing a Direct Lake on SQL table on a SQL view, which forces every query against it into fallback permanently.

g.aria-label: DirectQuery fallback trigger check (SQL flavor only)
g.title: DirectQuery fallback trigger check (SQL flavor only) — Direct Lake on SQL checks three documented conditions that force a fallback to DirectQuery.
g.text: Lakehouse-to-Power BI analytics on OneLake with Direct Lake

g.title: Report visual issues a query — A Power BI visual requests data, consumed exactly like any other semantic model.
g.text: Serve interactive Power BI reports over a Fabric lakehouse without copying or refreshing data into an import model, while staying inside one capacity's limits.

g.title: Framing (point-in-time anchor) — A metadata-only refresh that rebinds the model to the current Delta commit version, usually in seconds.

g.title: Column residency check — The engine checks whether requested columns are already resident in an in-memory cache.
g.text: Keep the model's resident column footprint under the SKU memory bound;

g.title: Lazy load from OneLake — Non-resident columns load directly from the OneLake Delta table, anchored to the last framing point.
g.text: otherwise queries may read columns from OneLake on demand.

g.aria-label: Trap: SQL views force permanent fallback
g.title: Trap: SQL views force permanent fallback — Basing a Direct Lake on SQL table on a view sends every query into DirectQuery fallback, invisibly.
